content:
A recent Apple job posting seems to hint that the company may have plans to launch some live Apple Fitness+ classes. However, I seriously doubt things are as straightforward as they appear.

The position is for a studio producer, and Apple is specifically looking for someone with extensive live production experience and a "genuine curiosity about the future direction of live content"...

MacRumors spotted the posting several weeks after it went live, and it does contain quite a few references to "live."

Apple Fitness+ is hiring a Producer who must have solid live or live-to-tape multi-camera production experience and a genuine curiosity about the future direction of live content. We are looking for a creative partner willing to experiment with new formats and push the boundaries of live fitness content to build the next generation of the Fitness+ experience—someone who can also build and maintain flexible schedules to accommodate the pace of a live production environment. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment and want to be part of the innovative team redefining live production at Apple, this is your chance to shine.

Some of the required qualifications also reinforce this direction.

  • Familiarity with both live production and post-production, with the ability to transition seamlessly between the two
  • Must be able to adapt to control room, office environments, and live event settings

Still, it's hard to see any advantage that live Fitness+ classes would have over pre-recorded ones. Apple's keynotes have taken the form of pre-recorded videos since the pandemic, and while some people may miss the tension of a live presentation, the prevailing view seems to be that this approach delivers a better experience.

At best, I could envision some real-time events being held on special occasions, but the actual fitness classes I would still expect to be pre-recorded. I think the biggest clues lie in the phrase "the pace of a live production environment," and the acceptance of live-to-tape experience. I suspect Apple wants to create that sense of excitement, even if the content ends up being pre-recorded.

What do you think? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
